Now that we have produced some parameters, it's possible to run some additional diagnostics, to check whether including real functions build on data breaks the model or not.

## Setup

Loading packages, data and the output of the models we just ran in the previous vignette. I will only pick one model, and not interpret any of the analyses. The scope is just to check if the model works and what we obtain makes sense.

```{r}
library(whereipm)
library(tidyverse)

# loading the data
data <- ipmdata

vitalRateModels <- readRDS(file.path(here::here(), "results", "vitalRateModels.rds"))
```

## Parameters and initial Population

I'm using here the same sets of space definitions I adopted in in the vignette [Model Diagnostics: Part I](DIPM-015_Model_diagnostics.html).

```{r}
# kernel paramters
kp <- create.kernel.params(L=-200, U=200, n.bins = 400)
kp.fine <- create.kernel.params(L=-200, U=200, n.bins = 800)
kp.coarse <- create.kernel.params(L=-200, U=200, n.bins = 100)

# populations
pop0 <- c(rep(0, kp$n.bins/2), rep(10,1), rep(0, kp$n.bins/2-1))
pop0.fine <- c(rep(0, kp.fine$n.bins/2), rep(10,1), rep(0, kp.fine$n.bins/2-1))
pop0.coarse <- c(rep(0, kp.coarse$n.bins/2), rep(10,1), rep(0, kp.coarse$n.bins/2-1))
```

For the vital parameters, I am using those obtained from the data pertaining to the late phase.

```{r, results = "asis"}
# First I need to extract the info in the model to make it easier to handle
Models <- vitalRateModels %>%
  transmute(
    survival = map(survival, broom::tidy),
    recruit = map(recruit, broom.mixed::tidy),
    adDispersal = map(adDispersal, broom::tidy),
    adDistance = map(adDistance, broom::tidy),
    natDispersal = map(natDispersal, broom::tidy),
    natDistance = map(natDistance, broom::tidy))

# Storing values into vital params list. By setting a value to i I can decide
# which phase to use. I'll try with the late for now.

i = 3

vp <- list(# Survival
                 s.int = Models$survival[[i]]%>%
                   filter(term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 s.slo = (Models$survival[[i]]%>%
                   filter(term == "s_loc_density") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 s.slo2 = returnIfExists(Models$survival[[i]]%>%
                   filter(term == "I(s_loc_density^2)") %>%
                   pull(estimate)),
                 s.multiplier = 1,
                 
                # Recruitment
                 r.int = Models$recruit[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          component == "zi",
                          term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 r.slo = (Models$recruit[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          component == "zi",
                          term == "s_loc_density") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 r.multiplier = 1,
                 f.int = Models$recruit[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          component == "cond",
                          term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 f.slo = (Models$recruit[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          component == "cond",
                          term == "s_loc_density") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 f.distribution = 'ztpoisson',
                 
                # Adult dispersal
                 p.stat.int.ad = Models$adDispersal[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 p.stat.slo.ad = (Models$adDispersal[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_loc_density") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 sigma.stat.ad = 0.25, 
                 mu.mob.int.ad = Models$adDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 mu.mob.slo.ad = (Models$adDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_loc_density") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 sigma.mob.ad = Models$adDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "ran_pars") %>%
                   pull(estimate) %>%
                   sum %>%
                   sqrt,
                 
                # Natal dispersal
                 p.stat.int.nat = Models$natDispersal[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 p.stat.slo.nat = (Models$natDispersal[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_loc_density.mid") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 p.stat.sloLand.nat = (Models$natDispersal[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_land_density.mid") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$land_density$scale,
                 p.stat.sloInt.nat = (Models$natDispersal[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_loc_density.mid:s_land_density.mid") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/(scalingAttr$loc_density$scale*scalingAttr$land_density$scale),
                 sigma.stat.nat = 0.25, 
                 mu.mob.int.nat = Models$natDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "(Intercept)") %>%
                   pull(estimate),
                 mu.mob.slo.nat = (Models$natDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_loc_density.mid") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale,
                 mu.mob.sloLand.nat = (Models$natDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_land_density.mid") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/scalingAttr$land_density$scale,
                 mu.mob.sloInt.nat = (Models$natDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "fixed",
                          term == "s_loc_density.mid:s_land_density.mid") %>%
                   pull(estimate))/(scalingAttr$loc_density$scale*scalingAttr$land_density$scale),
                 sigma.mob.nat = Models$natDistance[[i]]%>%
                   filter(effect == "ran_pars") %>%
                   pull(estimate) %>%
                   sum %>%
                   sqrt)
 
# replacing empty elements with zeros
vp <- lapply(vp, function(x) ifelse(length(x)==0,0,x))
```

## Running the model & Diagnostics

I can now run the IPM and alternate which real parts are added each time. First, I am adding the real vital parameters (but without using them) and repeat the simplest diagnostics ran earlier. The results should be identical, since the vp are not used.

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 12, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "1", rk = "0", gk = "still", nk = "still")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 12, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "1", rk = "0", gk = "still", nk = "still")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 12, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "1", rk = "0", gk = "still", nk = "still")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

### Dispersal

#### Everyone survives, a few are born...

I will test first if the redistribution kernels (for adult and natal dispersal) work. Keeping survival and reproduction at fixed values should allow to establish easily if the redistribution is working as intended.

I will also decrease the run time (from 12 to 6 months), to make things go faster. We now then expect the final population size (with perfect survival and one newborn every 2 adults) to grow to around `r round(10*1.5^6)`, given an initial population of 10 individuals.

#####...only adult dispersal

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "still")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "still")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "still")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

Looks ok.

#####...only natal dispersal

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "still", nk = "full")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "still", nk = "full")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "still", nk = "full")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

Also good.

#####...both adult and natal dispersal

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "full")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "full")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "1", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "full")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

When including both adult and natal dispersal, the final population size decreases to 113. This is due to a few fraction of individuals seeping out of the population limits and disappearing. The damage shouldn't be too bad though, since the previous population size, non rounded, was 10*1.5^6. This means probably only between 0.5 and 1 individuals were lost.


### Survival

I am now testing how the real survival behaves. This means including density-dependent survival. First, I am attempting to build a model with no dispersal, then adding the redistibution kernels back.

##### No dispersal

If no dispersal is possible, the model should fluctuate for a little (potentially) and then settle around an equilibrium generated by the population regulation operated by density-dependent survival IF there is negative density-dependent survival (high density - low survival). Here, it's not the case though, so the population will keep growing exponentially (due to the positive density-dependent survival).

The other expectation is that the final population size will be different in the 3 models. This is because initial density is different, generating a different expected survival. The coarser model will have lower density (same number of individuals in a larger bin size) and therefore is expected to have the smallest population size. The opposite will happen for the finer model.

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "full", rk = "small", gk = "still", nk = "still")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "full", rk = "small", gk = "still", nk = "still")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "full", rk = "small", gk = "still", nk = "still")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

The models behave as expected.

#### With Dispersal

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "full", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "full")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "full", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "full")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "full", rk = "small", gk = "full", nk = "full")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

### Recruitment

Finally, I am checking if recruitment works. This might not, since we are missing individuals that don't have assigned parentage, and we haven't corrected for that yet.  Recruitment might be too low and the population could go extinct.

I will try first having complete survival, which should allow the population to not go extinct and allow us to check if the density-dependent recruitment function works. Then I'll add dd survival, having therefore the complete realistic model based on the data.

#### No one dies on my watch

```{r}
IPM <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0, 
              sk = "1", rk = "full", gk = "full", nk = "full")

IPM.fine <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.fine, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.fine, 
              sk = "1", rk = "full", gk = "full", nk = "full")

IPM.coarse <- runIPM(kernel.params = kp.coarse, vital.params = vp,
              niter = 6, 
              init.pop = pop0.coarse, 
              sk = "1", rk = "full", gk = "full", nk = "full")

quick.plot(IPM, legend = "1m")
quick.plot(IPM.fine, legend = "0.5m")
quick.plot(IPM.coarse, legend = "2m")
```

Even with everyone surviving the population in the fine model is spread so thinly that there isn't a bin with at least one individual by month 4 (check the bottom left graph there).
